evergreen.text: just seen a girl making matcha in her kitchen with a fork. no whisk. no bowl. no sieve. no blank street. just her and a mug of green lumps going grey in the sink. Absolute soldier
evergreen.base_video: Creator sits at a kitchen counter holding their own iced drink, looking off camera and slowly raising the cup an inch like a toast, no smile.
evergreen.caption: a fork. against a whole bowl of matcha. who do you know like this
evergreen.why_this_brand: The fork-whisked clumpy matcha in a mug is the exact home-matcha failure the brand's matcha drinkers are escaping.
evergreen.what_changed: Cut 'she drank it standing up' so the fork and the lumpy mug stay the single image.

format.reason: Blank Street's pull is the relatable morning ritual, the clumpy fork-whisked matcha at home and the queue you don't have time for, which lands hardest as a silent reacting face plus one block of text about the old way. It also avoids needing brand-supplied demo footage, and app ordering is a behaviour change more than a thing to watch working.
format.why_not_runner_up: A drink being handed over is a weak demo and it needs footage the brand would have to shoot first.

evergreen.editor_fix: cut 'she drank it standing up' or the sink clause, one of the two is padding, and tighten so the fork stays the single image.

trend.text: just seen a girl trying to recreate the cinnamon bun matcha in her kitchen. no whisk. no sieve. no scales. no blank street. just a mug, a fork and a cinnamon jar she's shaking like it owes her money. tasting it off a spoon between attempts. Genuinely unwell
trend.caption: she's on attempt four. who do you know like this
trend.adaptation: Observed: the account posts dated drop announcements for named matcha flavours. Interpretation: people try to copy a drop at home. So the scene became recreating the site-listed Cinnamon Bun Matcha with a fork, not generic matcha.
trend.why_this_brand: Blank Street's autumn Cinnamon Bun Matcha is a named seasonal drink on the site, and the home version of it is exactly the clumpy fork-and-mug failure their matcha drinkers walk past on the way to work.
trend.source_evidence: COMING 17 JUNE Cookies and Cream Matcha.

alignment_review.reason: The reference is Blank Street's own drop-style announcements of named seasonal matcha flavours; the draft builds directly on that by dramatising someone trying to recreate one of those drops at home, and it names Cinnamon Bun Matcha, which is a site-listed autumn special (not invented). The adaptation note explains the link rather than sidestepping it, and the fork-in-a-mug scene matches the brand's stated old-way objects and scenes. No health, sourcing, price or competitor claims. Tone is deadpan rather than the brand's usual warm register, but that is a stylistic choice within bounds.
